slides.headline: The dairy swap was easy. The steps changed.
slides.photo_label: Original recipe licensed stock photo, not adapted dish

slides.headline: The list was the easy part
More chicken did not mean longer broiling
slides.rewrite: Two batches, 8 to 10 minutes per batch
slides.why: Uncrowded chicken keeps the char that balances the creamy sauce

slides.headline: Do not multiply the simmer
slides.instinct: Scale 10 to 15 minutes by the batch size
slides.rewrite: Start checking at 10 minutes, then use the spoon trail
slides.why: A wider pan evaporates liquid faster

slides.headline: Coconut yogurt needs a drip
slides.instinct: Move coated chicken straight to the tray
slides.rewrite: Let excess coconut yogurt drip off first
slides.why: The coating chars rather than pools

slides.headline: Simmer gently, then check the chicken
slides.instinct: Stretch the final simmer for the larger batch
slides.rewrite: Whisk smooth, simmer gently, check several pieces
slides.why: Separated coconut cream smooths out; chicken still has to reach 165°F

caption:
One swap can move the whole method. In this dairy-free chicken tikka masala, scaled from 4 to 6 servings, the ingredient list is simple: coconut yogurt, vegan butter, coconut cream. The steps are where cooks get burned. More chicken needs more broiler space, not a longer blast. A wider pan means you start checking the sauce at 10 minutes and look for the spoon trail. Coconut cream wants a gentle simmer. Chicken still needs 165°F in the thickest pieces. This is a real RecipeFix result, so the changed step comes with the reason.
